title: "About"

## Background

I studied English as an undergraduate and later completed a master's degree in
Linguistics at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. During my graduate studies,
I became increasingly interested in natural language processing, machine
learning, and software development.

Before coming to Vancouver, I worked as an AI Agent Engineer Intern at Covestro,
where I developed agentic AI applications using LangGraph, AWS Bedrock, MCP,
and retrieval-augmented generation. I also worked as an AI/ML Software Engineer
Intern at BMW, focusing on AI-assisted automotive testing, CAN bus data
processing, and workflow automation.

I am now studying in the Master of Data Science program at the University of
British Columbia. I came to Vancouver to strengthen my technical foundation
and prepare for a career in AI and software engineering.

## Why Data Science

My background in linguistics first introduced me to the challenge of turning
human language into structured information that computers can process.
As I explored NLP and large language models, I became more interested in
building complete AI systems rather than studying language alone.

I chose the MDSCL program to develop stronger skills in statistics, programming,
machine learning, and AI. I am particularly interested in building
reliable AI agents that can retrieve information, use external tools, analyze
data, and complete multi-step tasks. In the future, I hope to apply data science
and AI engineering to practical problems in industry.

## Outside of Data Science

Outside of data science, I enjoy cooking Chinese and Japanese food. Some of my
favorite dishes to make are gyudon, mapo tofu, Japanese curry, and tomato and
egg stir-fry. I also enjoy exploring Vancouver, trying local restaurants, and
discovering new neighborhoods.

I recently moved to Vancouver, so I am still learning about the city and
building a new life here. I especially enjoy its mild climate, diverse food,
and proximity to both the ocean and the mountains.
